en.title: The Avalanche visit a Leafs team stuck on three straight home losses
en.deck: Toronto has lost all three games of its homestand, scoring two goals or fewer each time, and was shut out 4-0 by New Jersey on Sunday. Colorado arrives at 10-6-2 after a 4-0 win over Detroit and is 10-2-0 when it scores three or more. The model and the market both make the Avalanche clear favourites.
news: Maple Leafs: Morgan Rielly and Jack Roslovic are day-to-day, and Colton Sissons left Sunday's game with a lower-body injury. Max Domi, Kirill Marchenko and Elvis Merzlikins are among eight players out.
Toronto has not named a starter. Sergei Bobrovsky (3-7-2, .886) played Saturday and Anthony Stolarz on Sunday.
Avalanche: Josh Manson is out about eight weeks with an ankle injury. Mackenzie Blackwood made 27 saves for his first shutout of the season against Detroit.
It is the first season for coach Jim Hiller and the new front office, and Toronto columnists now write that the honeymoon is over.
records: Gavin McKenna, the first overall pick in 2026, has 6 goals and 12 points in 19 games and is tied for the rookie scoring lead.
Auston Matthews leads Toronto with 27 points. His six-game point streak ended on Sunday.
Artturi Lehkonen has 12 goals, and Martin Necas had four points against Detroit. The model flags both as finishing above their usual rate.
Toronto won the first meeting 6-3 on Oct. 10. The last seven meetings averaged 7.1 goals.
betting: Market: Avalanche 1.62, Leafs 2.35, about 59–41 without the margin. The model has it 61–39, so the two agree. Toronto's unsettled goaltending is the open question.

Total: the market prices over 5.5 at 1.53 (about 62 %) and the model says 57 %. At 6.5 it is 52 % against 47 %. The model sits below the market on both lines, while the high-scoring head-to-head history sides with the market.
Player chances (model vs market, no margin): MacKinnon 1+ point 77 % vs 75 %, Makar 1+ point 66 % vs 62 %, Matthews 1+ point 65 % vs 64 %.

sv.title: Avalanche gästar ett Leafs som förlorat tre raka på hemmaplan
sv.deck: Toronto har förlorat alla tre matcherna på hemmaserien, med högst två gjorda mål i varje, och hölls mållöst av New Jersey (0-4) i söndags. Colorado kommer med 10-6-2 efter 4-0 mot Detroit och är 10-2-0 när laget gör minst tre mål. Både modellen och marknaden har Avalanche som klara favoriter.
news: Maple Leafs: Morgan Rielly och Jack Roslovic är osäkra, och Colton Sissons lämnade söndagens match med en skada i underkroppen. Max Domi, Kirill Marchenko och Elvis Merzlikins hör till de åtta som är borta.
Toronto har inte meddelat sin målvakt. Sergei Bobrovsky (3-7-2, ,886) spelade i lördags och Anthony Stolarz i söndags.
Avalanche: Josh Manson är borta i ungefär åtta veckor med en fotledsskada. Mackenzie Blackwood gjorde 27 räddningar och höll nollan mot Detroit för första gången i år.
Det är första säsongen för tränaren Jim Hiller och den nya ledningen, och krönikörerna i Toronto skriver nu att smekmånaden är över.

Artturi Lehkonen har 12 mål, och Martin Necas gjorde fyra poäng mot Detroit. Modellen flaggar att båda gör mål över sin vanliga nivå.
Toronto vann första mötet med 6-3 den 10 oktober. De sju senaste mötena hade i snitt 7,1 mål.

en.title: The Canadiens put a 10-game points run on the line against Kaprizov's Wild
en.deck: Montreal is 8-0-2 in its last 10 and has earned a point in 10 straight games. Minnesota is 12-3-4 and 6-1-3 in its last 10, with Kirill Kaprizov on 16 goals. The model and the market both see a coin flip in the first meeting of the season.
news: Canadiens: Ivan Demidov, who fractured his ankle in the preseason, is still a few weeks away. Mike Matheson is projected back around Nov. 14, and Sam Montembeault and Josh Anderson are out.
Jacob Fowler made 26 saves at Toronto for his eighth win and is the expected starter. Nick Suzuki returned from an upper-body injury on Nov. 5.

Wild: Brock Faber is cleared after skull surgery from a preseason puck to the head and is travelling with the team, but his return on this trip is not certain. Jared Spurgeon and Filip Gustavsson are out.
Jesper Wallstedt is expected in the Minnesota net.
records: Kaprizov has 16 goals and 31 points in 19 games.
Quinn Hughes, acquired from Vancouver last December, has 26 points (6 goals, 20 assists) in 19 games. The model flags his finishing as running hot.
Minnesota allows 2.3 goals a game, while 71 % of Montreal's games have gone over 5.5 goals.
The last six meetings averaged 5.8 goals.
betting: Market: Wild 1.84, Canadiens 2.00, about 52–48 without the margin. The model has the same split.

en.title: Ullmark may return as Ovechkin makes his second-to-last visit to Ottawa
en.deck: Linus Ullmark practised fully on Monday after missing eight games, and Ottawa will decide on Tuesday morning whether he starts. Alex Ovechkin, in his final season, needs one assist to tie Nicklas Backstrom's franchise record. Model and market both lean slightly to Ottawa.
news: Ullmark (lower body) is 7-1-0 with a .945 save percentage. If he sits, Samuel Ersson, who has won his last three starts, gets the net. The model's numbers assume Ullmark.
Ridly Greig returns from a lower-body injury. William Eklund, Warren Foegele and Andre Burakovsky are out for an extended period.
Tom Wilson is available: he got no further discipline after his game misconduct for boarding.
Logan Thompson is expected in goal for Washington. He is 6-1-1 with a .929 save percentage against Ottawa.
records: Ovechkin has one goal in 15 games and none in his last 10, but he has 39 goals in 63 career games against Ottawa.
Alex Tuch, who came from Buffalo in a sign-and-trade, leads Washington with 11 goals. The model flags Tuch and Jordan Kyrou as finishing hot.
13 of Washington's 15 games have gone over 5.5 goals, against half of Ottawa's.
Ottawa has won three of its last four.
betting: Market: Senators 1.76, Capitals 2.12, about 55–45 without the margin. The model has it 54–46, so they agree, but that rests on Ullmark starting.
Total: the market prices over 5.5 at 1.64 (about 58 %) and the model says 55 %. Washington's high-scoring games pull the other way.
Player chances (model vs market, no margin): Stützle 1+ point 67 % vs 65 %, Tuch 1+ point 55 % vs 48 % (the widest player gap in this game), Chabot 1+ point 43 % vs 43 %.

Ottawa har vunnit tre av de fyra senaste.

en.title: Hellebuyck sits out his return to Winnipeg as the Devils chase six straight
en.deck: Connor Hellebuyck, traded to New Jersey on Oct. 23, will not start in Winnipeg; Jake Allen gets the net. The Devils have won five straight, and Jack Hughes has five multi-point games in a row. The model is warmer on the Jets than the market is.
news: Devils GM Sunny Mehta called it an organizational decision, and coach Sheldon Keefe pointed to workload: three starts in six nights, with a home-and-home against Washington next. The Jets said they were disappointed.
Hellebuyck is 5-0-0 in New Jersey, and Sunday's shutout in Toronto was his 350th career win. Allen is 6-3-0 with an .881 save percentage.
Winnipeg got Dawson Mercer, Nico Daws and more in the trade. Josh Morrissey (wrist) is uncertain, and the Jets have not confirmed a starter.
Devils: Anthony Mantha will miss time after a high stick to the throat.
records: New Jersey goes for a sixth straight win and its 10th in 11 games.
Hughes has 25 points (9 goals, 16 assists) in 18 games, 11 of them in his last five.
Winnipeg has won three straight after a nine-game losing streak. Mark Scheifele scored the winner against Tampa Bay with two seconds left.
Kyle Connor leads the Jets with 13 goals.
betting: Market: Devils 1.66, Jets 2.28, about 58–42 without the margin. The model, with Allen in the Devils' net, has it 53–47: a clear gap toward Winnipeg.
Total: the market prices over 5.5 at 1.71 (about 56 %) and the model says the same. The last six meetings averaged 6.5 goals.

en.deck: Detroit and St. Louis have both lost three straight. The Red Wings have been outscored 10-3 in that run and play without Dylan Larkin, whom the club suspended after he left the team over a trade request. The model sees a much closer game than the market.
news: Larkin will not play unless he is traded, and Simon Edvinsson is an unsigned restricted free agent who wants a trade. Steve Yzerman was fired in July and Shawn Horcoff is interim GM.
